title: Interfaces Intro
concept: Interfaces define shared behavior that types can implement — like Eq for equality, Ord for ordering, Display for string output.
why: Without interfaces, every type would have its own method names. Interfaces provide a COMMON LANGUAGE for what types can do.
tips: Interfaces define WHAT a type can do, not HOW — they're contracts for behavior
A type can implement MANY interfaces — there's no limit
Think of interfaces as capabilities: T: Eq means 'T can be compared for equality'
Interfaces enable generic programming — write code against interfaces, not concrete types
common_mistakes: Confusing interfaces with classes/inheritance — they're more like capabilities
Defining interfaces that are too broad — each interface should have one clear purpose
Implementing interface methods that violate the interface's contract (e.g., Eq that's not symmetric)
